purpose: The documentation chrome, composed once in the app: a sticky header (the Azion Docs mark, the section links, `SearchTrigger` and the app's actions), the navigation rail (`Sidebar` + `Menu`) on the inline start, the article in the layout's `<main>`, the "On this page" rail (`DocOnThisPage`) on the inline end with its own slot below it, and the footer under the article. The **document** scrolls: the header and both rails are sticky, so a full-page capture shows the whole article, the browser's find and scroll restoration work, and the dark canvas is painted to the end. The outline follows the reading position, a jump clears the sticky header, and below `lg` the rail moves into a drawer opened from the header. The `Command` palette lists every navigation page. Doc pages are only their article, rendered through the default slot.
useWhen: Every documentation page (guide, reference, legal, changelog): put one `DocLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page's article as its default slot.
A docs site that needs the navigation rail, the outline and the search palette without hand-composing `GlobalHeader`, `Sidebar`, `Menu`, `DocOnThisPage`, `Drawer` and `Command`.
avoidWhen: A docs landing page with no rail (the docs home) → render it with `DocHero` and the sections, without this layout, or pass an empty `navigation` and `outline`.
related: DocOnThisPage` — the outline rail; `outline` and `outlineGroups` are bound onto it.
DocHeading` — headings whose anchor links the layout scrolls to, clearing the sticky header.
DocPageHeader`, `DocProse`, `DocPagination` — the article parts rendered in the default slot.
Sidebar`, `Menu` — the navigation rail; `navigation` is mapped onto `Menu` groups.
SearchTrigger`, `Command` — the header search and the palette it opens.
shells/documentation` — the block that shows this layout with a sample docs tree.
bestPractices: Compose the layout once, in the app's root; each route renders only its article. Never put a header, a rail or an inner scroll area in a page.
Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href` (an in-app path is followed with the router; never `to`); leave `activeId` empty so the current page follows the route.
Pass the page's headings as `outline` (`{ id, text, depth }`) with the same ids the `DocHeading`s carry; the layout tracks which one is in view.
Put the theme switch in `navigation-footer`, the GitHub and Console links in `actions`, a call to action (`DocCta`) in `aside`, and the site footer (`Footer kind="content"`) in `footer`.
The page renders no `<main>` and no `ScrollArea` around the article: the document scrolls.

A drill row (`kind: 'drill'`) opens its level in place; the rail's Back then reads `Back to Docs` at the first level. Set `rootLabel` when the tree is not the whole docs (`Back to API reference`); never add a hand-made Back row to `navigation`.
